skills.name: debug-web-app
skills.description: Diagnose reproducible web-app failures with evidence, isolate the smallest cause, apply a scoped fix, and verify the original symptom. Use for runtime errors, broken interactions, incorrect data flow, rendering failures, or regressions; do not use for speculative cleanup.

skills.name: build-tailwind-ui
skills.description: Build and refine interfaces in projects that already use Tailwind CSS. Use for responsive layout, project tokens, state variants, dark mode, shadcn-style components, and maintainable class composition; do not use to choose the product's overall art direction.

skills.name: build-accessible-ui
skills.description: Build or repair accessible web interfaces using native semantics, keyboard and focus behavior, clear forms, perceivable states, and appropriate ARIA. Use when implementing or reviewing interactive UI; pair it with the project's existing accessibility and browser requirements.

skills.name: write-safe-typescript
skills.description: Write and refactor TypeScript with trustworthy boundary validation, narrowing, discriminated unions, useful inference, safe async flows, and readable public types. Use when type design or unsafe data handling materially affects correctness; avoid type-level machinery without a concrete payoff.

skills.name: art-direct-web
skills.description: Art-direct marketing sites, landing pages, portfolios, editorial pages, and campaign experiences from a concrete brief. Use when visual narrative, composition, typography, imagery, and motion are central; use design-product-ui instead for routine application workflows.

skills.name: design-product-ui
skills.description: Design and implement product interfaces such as dashboards, settings, forms, data views, and multi-step workflows. Use for hierarchy, density, navigation, interaction states, responsive behavior, and accessible product UI; use art-direct-web for marketing-led experiences.

skills.name: review-code
skills.description: Review a requested diff, file set, or repository scope for concrete correctness, security, performance, reliability, and maintainability problems. Use when the user wants findings or merge confidence; report only unless fixes or external actions are explicitly requested.

skills.name: simplify-code
skills.description: Simplify user-selected or newly changed code while preserving observable behavior and established contracts. Use to reduce unnecessary nesting, duplication, indirection, or cleverness in a bounded area; do not turn a focused cleanup into a broad refactor.
